Title: Julius Odeke’s Story of Transformation
NewsSummary: Julius credits GSMC with significantly sharpening his skills and broadening his worldview
NewsContent:
​

When Julius Odeke decided to pursue a Master of Arts in Digital Journalism (MADJ) at the Aga Khan University Graduate School of Media and Communications (GSMC), it was more than an academic decision; it was a profound turning point. 

Hailing from a region deeply affected by conflict, Julius was drawn to GSMC’s stellar reputation, inclusive environment, and the promise of financial aid.. "The opportunity to engage with renowned faculty and a diverse student body, along with the potential for career growth, made GSMC a clear choice," he shares.

His journey at GSMC was filled with memorable moments, especially the unexpected impact of a student award. "It didn’t seem like a big award at the time," he recalls, "but it ended up changing everything." A generous donor in the UK, touched by Julius’ story, offered to cover his outstanding tuition. This act of kindness reinforced his belief in the power of recognition and community. He also speaks fondly of the inspiration and mentorship he received from faculty like Professor Peter Kimani and Mr Joseph Warungu, whose guidance was instrumental in his professional growth.

Like many working professionals returning to school, Julius faced his share of challenges, including needing to retake two courses. Yet, with discipline and determination, he overcame these hurdles. "As a journalist, I’m used to deadlines," he explains. "I also don’t go out much, so I made time for study and work." His ability to effectively balance his responsibilities was key to his academic success.

Today, Julius credits GSMC with significantly sharpening his skills and broadening his worldview. His time at AKU fostered a greater appreciation for cultural diversity and enhanced his journalistic practice, particularly in investigative writing and photojournalism. "In 2023, I was ranked among the best photographers in Uganda by the Uganda Photography Press Association," he proudly notes, attributing this recognition to the practical training he received at GSMC.

Looking ahead, Julius dreams of earning a PhD and eventually returning to GSMC as faculty. "I’ve already recommended several students to the university," he says, "because it offers hands-on, real-world journalism training." 

For him, GSMC is more than just an institution; it is a launching pad. As he aptly puts it: "The GSMC is a world-class academic institution that strives for excellence — and it shows in the success of its alumni."
